author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR25466; PTN002402215 (gain of T cell costimulation, GO:0031295); PTN002402215 (gain of positive regulation of T cell proliferation, GO:0042102)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:Q9BQ51 PDCD1LG2 (programmed cell death 1 ligand 2)

* **Type of Issue:** Erroneous propagation from paralogs (T cell costimulation). For positive regulation of T cell proliferation the evidence conflicts, and one source (rat Cd274) looks inverted.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


*The same node PTN002402215 also passes on the opposite term, negative regulation of T cell proliferation ([GO:0042130](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0042130)), to PDCD1LG2, CD274, CD80 and CD86. Its evidence includes human PDCD1LG2 and mouse Pdcd1lg2, so the node carries both directions, each with Pdcd1lg2 as evidence. Mouse Pdcd1lg2's own annotations also go both ways: positive regulation of T cell proliferation (IDA, [PMID:11283156](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11283156/)) and negative regulation (IDA, [PMID:11224527](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11224527/) and [PMID:17016562](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17016562/)).*

**Inherited:** PDCD1LG2 `involved_in` *T cell costimulation* ([GO:0031295](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0031295))

- **Gain:** PTN002402215 (speciation, Deuterostomia; human genes below: CD274, CD80, CD86, PDCD1LG2), dated 2017-04-20.
- **Evidence genes (2):** Cd80 (MOUSE), CD274 (HUMAN).
- **Relation to PDCD1LG2:** paralogs: Cd80 (MOUSE), CD274 (HUMAN).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** CD274, CD80, CD86.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** same annotation, from PTN002402215.

**Inherited:** PDCD1LG2 `involved_in` *positive regulation of T cell proliferation* ([GO:0042102](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0042102))

- **Gain:** PTN002402215 (speciation, Deuterostomia; human genes below: CD274, CD80, CD86, PDCD1LG2), dated 2017-04-20.
- **Evidence genes (6):** Cd86 (MOUSE), Cd80 (MOUSE), Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE), Cd274 (RAT), Cd80 (RAT), Cd86 (RAT).
- **Relation to PDCD1LG2:** orthologs: Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE); paralogs: Cd86 (MOUSE), Cd80 (MOUSE), Cd274 (RAT), Cd80 (RAT), Cd86 (RAT).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** CD274, CD80, CD86.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** same annotation, from PTN002402215.

**PDCD1LG2's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *T cell costimulation*: 2 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *negative regulation of activated T cell proliferation* ([GO:0046007](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0046007)): [PMID:12538684](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12538684/) (IMP)
- *negative regulation of T cell activation* ([GO:0050868](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0050868)): [PMID:11224527](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11224527/) (IDA)

**PDCD1LG2's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *positive regulation of T cell proliferation*: 2 opposing, 0 supporting (same as above).


**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 30 sentences mention PDCD1LG2 together with *T cell activation*. By cue words, 12 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 6 agree.

> **Discussion PD-1 and its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 are critical for tolerance and immune homeostasis by inhibiting T-cell activation.**

— Liu C, Jiang J, Gao L, Wang X, Hu X, Wu M et al. (2015). Soluble PD-1 aggravates progression of collagen-induced arthritis through Th1 and Th17 pathways. *Arthritis research & therapy*. [PMID:26608464](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26608464/).


> PD-L1 is widely expressed on hematopoietic cells and non-hematopoietic cells, while PD-L2 expression is restricted to DC, macrophages, B1 B cells, and mast cells. **PD-L2 signaling through PD-1 has been characterized as an inhibitory interaction, but there is also evidence that PD-L2 expression on DC is important in activation of naïve T cells.** In concordance with previous reports of the downregulation of PD-L2 in the presence of IL-10 on BM-derived DC and consistent with a potential activation function, cDC but not DCreg express high levels of PD-L2 (Figures 1B and 2).

— Scroggins SM, Olivier AK, Meyerholz DK, Schlueter AJ (2013). Characterization of regulatory dendritic cells that mitigate acute graft-versus-host disease in older mice following allogeneic bone marrow transplantation. *PloS one*. [PMID:24040397](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24040397/).


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (6): none of them clearly describes PD-L2 as costimulatory. Three say that PD-1 engagement by its ligands inhibits T cells; the others are about T cell exhaustion, say the pathway both activates and inhibits T cells, or are about PD-1 expression.

**Sentences counted as agreeing with *positive regulation of T cell proliferation*** (6 of 22 sentences mentioning PDCD1LG2 with *T cell proliferation*; 13 against): four of them, from three papers, report that PD-L2 can drive T cell proliferation, in some studies independently of PD-1. So the positive term has some support. The other two describe inhibition. Two examples:

> There is considerable evidence that PD-L2 inhibits immunity by binding to the PD-1 co-inhibitory receptor (Latchman et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2006). **However, several studies have shown that PD-L2 can function to stimulate T cell proliferation and cytokine production, even in PD-1–deficient T cells or with PD-L2 mutants that did not bind to PD-1 (Liu et al., 2003; Shin et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2003).** These findings suggest that PD-L2 may function through a receptor other than PD-1.

— Xiao Y, Yu S, Zhu B, Bedoret D, Bu X, Francisco LM et al. (2014). RGMb is a novel binding partner for PD-L2 and its engagement with PD-L2 promotes respiratory tolerance. *The Journal of experimental medicine*. [PMID:24752301](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24752301/).


> A number of infection studies with viral and fungal pathogens reported that PD-1:PD-L1 interactions inhibit T and B cell proliferation and blocking these interactions significantly rescues T cell functions and host resistance to infections. **Conversely, however, some studies also report that PD-1:PD-L2 (B7-DC) interactions can drive the proliferation of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.** The PD-1: PD-L1 axis has been shown to be important for bacterial pathogens as well.

— Vashishta M, Khan N, Mehto S, Sehgal D, Natarajan K (2015). Pneumococal Surface Protein A (PspA) Regulates Programmed Death Ligand 1 Expression on Dendritic Cells in a Toll-Like Receptor 2 and Calcium Dependent Manner. *PloS one*. [PMID:26214513](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26214513/).


**Reasoning on *T cell costimulation*** (evidence-cited; verdict *error likely*, high confidence; cause: paralog inheritance): T cell costimulation is defined as a second signal that augments T cell activation, but PDCD1LG2's own experiments (IDA and IMP) and the literature consistently describe PD-L2 as delivering inhibitory signals that restrain T cell activation and proliferation. The term rests only on paralogs (mouse Cd80, human CD274) that PDCD1LG2 meets at a duplication node, so the inheritance likely carried a costimulatory function onto an inhibitory ligand.

- *Context:* The GO term T cell costimulation is defined as a second signal via receptor-ligand pairs that augments T cell activation, i.e. a positive-direction process. (GO definition)
- *Against:* PDCD1LG2's own direct experiment (IDA) annotates it to negative regulation of T cell activation, and a loss-of-function experiment (IMP) to negative regulation of activated T cell proliferation. ([PMID:11224527](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11224527/); [PMID:12538684](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12538684/))
- *Against:* Reviews and primary-study sentences state that PD-1 and its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 deliver inhibitory signals and inhibit T cell activation and cytokine production, and Reactome places PD-L2 in co-inhibition by PD-1. (Keir et al. 2008; Liu C et al. 2015; Keir et al. 2006; Wang et al. 2021; Reactome)
- *Against:* Both evidence genes are paralogs (mouse Cd80, human CD274) and PDCD1LG2 meets them at a duplication node, so no ortholog of PDCD1LG2 supports the term. (Cd80; CD274; PANTHER tree)
- *For:* PD-L2 is a surface-bound ligand of a T cell receptor-ligand pair, matching the 'surface-bound receptor-ligand pairs' part of the definition, which may explain why the family-level annotation was placed. (GO definition; Wang et al. 2021)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Add a loss of T cell costimulation ([GO:0031295](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0031295)) at the PDCD1LG2 clade (PTN001978964); also review whether the CD274 experimental annotation to T cell costimulation is directionally correct. *Tree check:* A loss at PTN001978964 would also cover Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE), which was reported as costimulatory (IDA to positive regulation of T cell proliferation, [PMID:11283156](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11283156/)).

**Reasoning on *positive regulation of T cell proliferation*** (verdict *error possible*, medium confidence; cause: ortholog annotation conflict): PDCD1LG2's own direct experiments (two papers), six literature sentences and its Reactome pathway all show PD-L2 inhibiting T cell activation and proliferation through PD-1, the opposite of the inherited 'positive regulation of T cell proliferation'. The term was gained above the duplication that split the PD-L ligands from the costimulatory CD80/CD86, and most evidence genes are those paralogs. But the mouse Pdcd1lg2 ortholog is itself an evidence gene, so some experimental support for a positive effect exists, which leaves real uncertainty.

*Note on the reasoning:* The pack for the second term held six inhibitory sentences only. The sentences counted as agreeing above show that some studies report PD-L2 driving T cell proliferation, and mouse Pdcd1lg2 has an IDA for it (see the note at the top).

**Suggested change:**

- Add a loss (NOT) of *T cell costimulation* at **PTN000715277** (speciation, Catarrhini; human genes below: PDCD1LG2). PDCD1LG2's lineage meets the evidence genes only at gene duplications (CD274 (HUMAN) at PTN000715367; Cd80 (MOUSE) at PTN008619493), so the function may have diverged after duplication. It sits below Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE) rather than at PTN001978964, because Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE) is not an evidence gene but was reported as costimulatory (IDA to positive regulation of T cell proliferation, [PMID:11283156](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11283156/)). Nothing shows the primate genes diverging from mouse Pdcd1lg2, so review the mouse annotation before adding the loss.
- *positive regulation of T cell proliferation* rests on 6 evidence genes: 5 paralogs (Cd86 (MOUSE), Cd80 (MOUSE), Cd274 (RAT), Cd80 (RAT), Cd86 (RAT)) and 1 ortholog (Pdcd1lg2 (MOUSE)). Because an ortholog is among them, a loss on PDCD1LG2's branch would contradict that ortholog's annotation. Review those source annotations, or whether this term should propagate.
- One source of *positive regulation of T cell proliferation* looks inverted: rat Cd274 (IMP, [PMID:21717117](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21717117/)) comes from a paper showing that B7-H1 on hepatic stellate cells suppresses T-cell proliferation. The CD274 source of *T cell costimulation* (IDA, [PMID:10581077](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10581077/)) matches its paper, an early report of co-stimulation; the problem there is the term's propagation, not that annotation.

### References
- Keir ME, Butte MJ, Freeman GJ, Sharpe AH (2008). PD-1 and its ligands in tolerance and immunity. *Annu Rev Immunol*. [PMID:18173375](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18173375/).
- Keir ME, Liang SC, Guleria I, Latchman YE, Qipo A, Albacker LA et al. (2006). Tissue expression of PD-L1 mediates peripheral T cell tolerance. *The Journal of experimental medicine*. [PMID:16606670](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16606670/).
- Liu C, Jiang J, Gao L, Wang X, Hu X, Wu M et al. (2015). Soluble PD-1 aggravates progression of collagen-induced arthritis through Th1 and Th17 pathways. *Arthritis research & therapy*. [PMID:26608464](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26608464/).
- Scroggins SM, Olivier AK, Meyerholz DK, Schlueter AJ (2013). Characterization of regulatory dendritic cells that mitigate acute graft-versus-host disease in older mice following allogeneic bone marrow transplantation. *PloS one*. [PMID:24040397](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24040397/).
- Vashishta M, Khan N, Mehto S, Sehgal D, Natarajan K (2015). Pneumococal Surface Protein A (PspA) Regulates Programmed Death Ligand 1 Expression on Dendritic Cells in a Toll-Like Receptor 2 and Calcium Dependent Manner. *PloS one*. [PMID:26214513](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26214513/).
- Wang Q, Bardhan K, Boussiotis VA, Patsoukis N (2021). The PD-1 Interactome. *Adv Biol (Weinh)*. [PMID:34170628](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34170628/).
- Xiao Y, Yu S, Zhu B, Bedoret D, Bu X, Francisco LM et al. (2014). RGMb is a novel binding partner for PD-L2 and its engagement with PD-L2 promotes respiratory tolerance. *The Journal of experimental medicine*. [PMID:24752301](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24752301/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR25466: PDCD1LG2 inherits "T cell costimulation" and "positive regulation of T cell proliferation", contrary to its own experimental annotations

author: goldturtle
body:
Update after checking the latest annotation data: this was already addressed.

In the UniProt-GOA human file of 2026-11-04, PDCD1LG2 no longer has the IBAs to *T cell costimulation* (GO:0031295), *positive regulation of T cell proliferation* (GO:0042102) or *negative regulation of T cell proliferation* (GO:0042130). The family (PTHR25466) was re-annotated on 2026-02-24: PDCD1LG2 now has new IBAs from PTN002402215, PTN002816546 and PTN008406010, and CD274, CD80 and CD86 no longer have these terms either. Our analysis used the PAN-GO 2025-10-12 release, which predates that change, so we missed it.

One related point is not a PAN-GO matter: rat Cd274's IMP to *positive regulation of T cell proliferation* (RGD, PMID:21717117) looks inverted relative to its paper.

Sorry for the noise. Closing.
